title: MEP-CMAP Analyser

creators.name: Andrushko, Justin W.
creators.affiliation: School of Sport, Exercise and Rehabilitation, Northumbria University, Newcastle upon Tyne, UK

description:
MEP-CMAP Analyser is a BIDS-compliant, open-source, cross-platform desktop application for processing, quantifying and group-analysing transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) and electromyography (EMG) neurophysiology recordings. It is built for researchers who need reproducible, auditable waveform analysis without writing custom scripts for every study.

The tool is not limited to a single measure or paradigm. It handles motor evoked potentials (MEPs), compound muscle action potentials (CMAPs), cortical silent periods (cSPs), M-wave recruitment curves, paired-pulse protocols such as short-interval intracortical inhibition (SICI) and intracortical facilitation (ICF), and any other time-locked EMG response measurable by peak-to-peak amplitude, onset latency or area under the curve. It operates on continuous recordings, pre-epoched trial stacks, and EMG bursts recorded without stimulation.

Capabilities

  • Direct import of Spike2, LabChart, EDF/BDF, AcqKnowledge and generic delimited text files, with a guided one-time wizard for arbitrary tabular layouts
  • Configurable filtering, including band-pass, notch and harmonic suppression, with live preview
  • Automated detection of response onset, peak-to-peak amplitude, area under the curve and cortical silent period duration, each overridable per trial
  • Automated outlier screening with an interactive review step, so exclusion decisions are explicit, persistent and recorded in the output
  • An interactive per-trial data inspector for marker adjustment, annotation and exclusion
  • Mmax normalisation with robust plateau detection across full recruitment curves, supramaximal clusters or a single M-wave
  • Compensation of evoked-potential magnitude for pre-stimulus spinal motoneurone excitability by quantile regression, following the method of Carson (2026, Journal of Physiology 604.14, 5731-5757), verified against the author's published reference implementation
  • Paired-pulse ratio computation with multiple reference assignments per file
  • Trial-level and summary CSV output, a group-level file formatted for linear mixed-effects modelling, per-trial waveform bundles, and BIDS-style derivatives with provenance

Changes in version 1.3.0

  • New temporal MEP decomposition add-on. Each motor evoked potential is divided into successive time bins measured from its onset (2 ms by default) and aggregated into an early and a late phase, following the approach used to dissociate fast-conducting corticospinal from slower, polysynaptic cortico-reticulospinal transmission. The analysis window is clamped to the detected MEP offset so the late phase cannot extend into the cortical silent period, background electromyographic activity is subtracted over each window in proportion to its duration, and per-condition diagnostic figures show the onset-aligned mean rectified trace together with the mean bin profile. Bin width, window length and the early/late boundary are user settings; the bin profile is the primary output and the phase split is derived from it.
  • Per-trial add-on outputs are now joined onto the group-level table automatically. Any add-on writing the File, StimType and Segment keys alongside its measurements is merged into the second-level export without configuration. The join is additive: core measurements are never overwritten, a column whose name clashes with an existing one is namespaced after its add-on rather than discarded, and a sidecar whose keys match no trials is skipped with a note instead of appending empty columns.
  • The MEPFeatX add-on now emits a one-based Segment key matching the core per-trial table and reports the source file name rather than the BIDS prefix, so its morphological features reach the group table. The existing zero-based Trial index is retained.
  • Bin-edge integration is evaluated against the signal interpolated at the exact edge rather than at the nearest sample, so bin boundaries are not quantised to the sampling grid.
  • Expanded automated test coverage for the new add-on and for the group-level join.

Note on reproducibility: this release adds new outputs and does not alter any existing measurement, so results produced by version 1.2.9 are unchanged and no reprocessing is required. Datasets analysed with the excitability compensation in version 1.2.5 or earlier should still be reprocessed, as noted for version 1.2.8.

Source code: https://github.com/jandrushko/mep-cmap-analyser
Python package: https://pypi.org/project/mep-cmap-analyser/
Licence: MIT
Requirements: Python 3.9 or later; pre-built binaries are provided for Windows, macOS and Linux.
